correctness.rationale: Unit-edge hat products have integrals 1/3 at a given endpoint and 1/6 across the edge. Thus Q=6M=2dI+A with d=(r−1)s. If H averages within each part and J/(rs) averages globally, the orthogonal blocks I−H, H−J/(rs), J/(rs) have eigenvalues 2d, st, 3d in Q. Inverting them gives the displayed rows β(3st+1), β, −2β. The evaluation kernel interpolates those rows multiplied by six. It integrates to one because the projector preserves constants. With T=3st+1 its negative mass is 12βd/(T+2)+4β(s−1)d+12β choose(r−1,2)s², obtained from the negative triangles on the first two edge classes and the constant negative value on the third. One plus twice this mass simplifies to 2+1/(3t)−4/(3(ts+1)), the stated formula. The sign input can be set to either unit sign on any zeros. Values at a vertex yield sharp essential supremum because the output is continuous and incident edges have positive measure arbitrarily close to it. For any interior evaluation on vw, the two endpoint kernels have opposite signs on a positive-length subinterval of the source edge vw near v, so its nontrivial convex interpolation has strictly smaller L¹ norm. The threshold follows from t(s−4)+1. Differentiating the simplified expression gives 4t/[3(ts+1)²] in s and −1/(3t²)+4s/[3(ts+1)²] in t; at t≥3 the latter is positive for s=2,3 and negative for s≥4. This gives the unique minimum 121/63 at (3,2); the two stated limits and the bound approached at r=3 as s grows give the unattained supremum 19/9.

Its proof gives the same three kernel entries. Strict exclusion of interior evaluations is an immediate consequence of those entries on the edge of evaluation itself. The monotonicity in r and the restricted envelope are direct algebraic consequences of the already stated formula and limits. Demonstrable indexed coverage and these implications exhaust the substantive claim; index date is not used to determine authorship or historical priority.
